what_this_pins: The edge-extend tool offers FIVE independently switchable viewport handle banks -- move, rotate, scale, plane and local -- and only the MOVE bank is on by default. A tool that always draws move+rotate+scale draws two banks the reference editor does not.

Every handle is a way of writing the tool's own parameters. A handle drag sets (parameter value at drag start) + (gesture delta) on the same parameters the properties panel edits, and the geometry is then a re-evaluation of the one kernel from the untouched source cage. No handle transforms geometry or the selection directly.

The rotate/scale pivot is the CENTRE OF THE BOUNDING BOX of the selected vertices -- a bounding-box mid, not a vertex centroid, and not the action centre. Forcing the action centre to the world origin does not move it.

That pivot is computed once when the tool is initialised in a viewport and is not recomputed per evaluation. The non-interactive command path never initialises it and therefore pivots at the world origin.
Scale parameters written by a scale handle are clamped at zero: the drag cannot push a scale negative.

rotate.note: one Euler component per ring; part 203 is a screen-axis ring that writes all three at once via an axis-angle matrix decomposed to XYZ Euler, and is drawn only in a view with no principal axis

scale.note: value written is max(0, base + delta)

plane.note: writes the two components lying in the chosen plane; the third is skipped

rig.description: Open 5-vertex, 2-triangle mesh placed off the origin with no axis-aligned edge and no face normal along a world axis. The two selected edges share one vertex and differ in length by about 13x, so the selected subset's bounding-box mid and its vertex centroid are far apart; the two unselected vertices push the whole-mesh bounding box away from the selected subset's.

cases.name: interactive_rotate_pivot
cases.path: tool armed in a viewport, then rotate parameters set
cases.rotation_order: Rx then Ry then Rz (matrix product Rz*Ry*Rx)
cases.new_ring_note: one vertex per distinct selected vertex; the shared vertex welds to a single new vertex used by both bridge quads
cases.action_centre_control: repeating the case with the action centre forced to the world origin gives the same pivot, bit for bit

cases.name: command_path_rotate_pivot

cases.note: this is the CONTROL: the same tool, same parameters, same rig, and the pivot field is simply never populated on this path
